item.title: Sqwod Daily — Wednesday, 29 July 2026
item.description: What if your membership pricing is accidentally optimized for your next investor conversation instead of your next renewal?
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 29 July 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Wednesday, 29 July 2026 · Weekday
What if your membership pricing is accidentally optimized for your next investor conversation instead of your next renewal?
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
Throne Science
 $10M
seed round to build a gut-health monitoring toilet, co-founded by Whoop's former CTO
Connect the dots
When your pricing model serves the deck, not the member
The $19.99 car wash play is a masterclass in recurring-revenue theater: low price = high signup volume = beautiful MRR chart = happy investors. The cars may or may not get clean. Sound familiar? Fitness memberships can fall into exactly the same trap — architect your tiers around churn metrics and cohort retention curves for a future raise, and you quietly stop asking whether the product actually solves the member's problem week to week.
The so-what: audit your membership structure this quarter with one brutal question — 'Would I design this the same way if I never planned to raise money or sell?' If the answer is no, your pricing architecture is sending the wrong signal to your most valuable asset: the people who actually show up. Retention isn't a metric you report; it's a feeling your members have on the way home.
The rundown
01
$19.99/Month Car Washes Are Really Selling Wall Street a Subscription
The Auto Wire flags that cheap car wash memberships are engineered for investor metrics, not clean cars — a useful reminder that any recurring-revenue model can be built around the pitch deck rather than the customer.
Source: The Auto Wire →
02
100 More Gyms: FitActive Is Dead Serious About Italy
The Italian chain just reaffirmed plans to open 100 additional locations, doubling down on ambitions it first laid out at the ATN Summit. If you're watching European fitness expansion, this one's worth a spot on your radar.
Source: Athletech News →
03
$10M to track gut health — from the toilet
Throne Science, co-founded by Whoop's former CTO, just raised $10M to turn your porcelain throne into a health monitor. If your clients are asking about recovery and readiness, gut data from the bathroom might be the next frontier worth watching.
Source: Crunchbase News →
04
Preston fitness firms merge gym, Pilates & recovery for women
A group of Preston fitness businesses has launched a combined women's wellness membership spanning gym access, Pilates, and recovery. For operators eyeing retention, bundled multi-modal memberships are clearly becoming the move worth watching.
Source: Blog Preston →
05
Community gym crowdfunds to beat the heat (and the chill)
Wheathampstead's community gym has launched a Crowdfunder campaign to keep its space comfortable year-round — a reminder that member retention isn't just programming, it's also not sweating through a session in July or freezing in January.
Source: St Albans Times →
06
Mojawa's Purra Flow headphones now coach your clients mid-rep
The new AI-powered bone conduction headphones from Mojawa deliver real-time coaching audio through the skull — not the ears — while workouts happen. For trainers and studio operators, it's a front-row seat to what on-demand, wearable coaching actually looks like at the consumer level.
Source: The Manila Times →
Stat
100
additional gym locations FitActive plans to open in Italy
European fitness expansion is far from saturated — FitActive doubling its footprint signals that mid-market, high-volume club models still have serious runway on the continent.
Sqwod recs
✓ Steal: Run a 'member effort score' survey: one question — 'How easy is it to get value from your membership?' — sent 30 days post-signup. Low scores predict churn weeks before it shows in your data.
✓ Track: Start logging your monthly revenue-per-active-member alongside total MRR — it exposes whether growth is real or just volume masking declining engagement per head.
✓ Try: Map one 'uncomfortable physical moment' in your facility — temperature, noise, parking, lighting — and fix it before adding any new programming. Environment retention is invisible until it isn't.

item.description: The most scalable thing in your studio might not be your square footage — it's the person teaching in it.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 28 July 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Tuesday, 28 July 2026 · Weekday
The most scalable thing in your studio might not be your square footage — it's the person teaching in it.
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
VEYR
 £1M
UK startup raising to bring AI-powered fitness coaching to market
Connect the dots
Your talent pipeline beats your franchise deck
One LA Pilates studio is quietly doing what most growth-obsessed operators won't: investing in developing instructors instead of opening new doors. It sounds counterintuitive until you realise that franchises export your brand but dilute your culture, while great instructors multiply your culture and carry it into every room they ever teach in. The constraint was never capital — it was people who truly get it.
For studio founders, this reframes the whole expansion question. Before you model out a second location, ask what your instructor development pipeline actually looks like. If your best teachers leave because there's no upward path, you're not scaling — you're churning. The studios that crack retention (member and staff) tend to be the ones that treat instructor growth as a product, not a perk.
The rundown
01
VEYR is raising £1M to bring AI coaching to fitness
The UK startup just launched a £1 million funding round for AI-powered fitness coaching — a signal that investors are betting the next great personal trainer might not need a locker room.
Source: Well Nation →
02
People First: The Secret Behind All-Inclusive Fitness Success
body LIFE breaks down why putting people before programming is the real growth lever in all-inclusive fitness — useful reading if you're wondering why your retention numbers aren't matching your membership numbers.
Source: body LIFE →
03
Float Like a Butterfly, Lift Like a Legend
Luxury fitness brand Pent has launched an equipment collection with the Muhammad Ali Estate, per Business Traveller — and for operators looking to give their floor a serious prestige upgrade, this collab signals that heritage IP is becoming the new premium differentiator in fitness hardware.
Source: Business Traveller →
04
This LA Pilates Studio Is Scaling Instructors, Not Franchises
While competitors chase franchise growth, one LA Pilates studio is betting that developing instructors is the real expansion play. For studio owners, it's a timely reminder that your talent pipeline might be your most scalable asset.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Aging Well Is Big Business — Is Your Marketing Keeping Up?
The Global Wellness Institute is putting a spotlight on the 'Aging Well' category and how brands are (finally) advertising to older adults seriously. If your studio still treats 50+ as an afterthought, you're leaving a very fit, very motivated demographic on the table.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
06
Oura Ring 4: Great life coach, middling gym buddy
GB News finds the Oura Ring 4 excels at tracking lifestyle habits but falls short as a serious training tool — worth knowing before you recommend it to a client who wants performance data, not just pretty sleep scores.
Source: GB News →
Sqwod recs
✓ Track: Start measuring instructor tenure alongside member retention — if your staff churn rate is high, your member churn will follow within 90 days. Run the numbers monthly.
✓ Steal: Create a simple '50+ onboarding script' for your front desk: different language, different goals, different wins than a 30-year-old. Older adults respond to capability framing ('what you'll be able to do') over aesthetics — update your intake form to reflect that.
✓ Try: Run a 30-minute 'teach-back' session monthly where junior instructors coach a segment in front of peers — it accelerates development faster than shadowing alone and costs nothing but calendar time.

item.description: When a hardware giant buys the software your clients plan their lives around, 'platform risk' stops being a buzzword.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 23 July 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Thursday, 23 July 2026 · Weekday
When a hardware giant buys the software your clients plan their lives around, 'platform risk' stops being a buzzword.
— Sqwod
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Garmin / TrainingPeaks

Garmin acquires TrainingPeaks, raising questions about platform pricing, integrations, and data ownership for coaches
Connect the dots
Garmin + TrainingPeaks: who really owns your programming?
TrainingPeaks has long been the invisible backbone of serious training — coaches build plans there, athletes live there, and everyone quietly assumed it would stay neutral. Garmin just ended that assumption. An acquisition folds a software platform into a hardware ecosystem, and the history of those mergers is pretty consistent: integrations tighten, pricing evolves, and the new parent's devices get the best data treatment first.
For studio operators and coaches, the concrete risk is dependency. If your entire client programming stack lives in one platform that now answers to a device manufacturer, your leverage just shrank. This week's action is simple: audit where your programming actually lives. Do you have exportable copies? Are your athletes locked to a Garmin-native experience to get full value? Diversification isn't paranoia — it's ops hygiene.
The rundown
01
$200 Screenless: Garmin Takes a Shot at Whoop's Wrist
Garmin just dropped a $200 screen-free fitness band aimed squarely at Whoop's territory. For coaches and studio operators who recommend wearables to clients, there's a new name in the no-display game worth knowing.
Source: Athletech News →
02
DSSV drops 2026 DACH fitness industry benchmarks
The DSSV has unveiled the key figures shaping the German-speaking fitness market in 2026. If you run a gym or coach clients in the region, this is the data that tells you where the money and membership trends are actually heading.
Source: DSSV →
03
body LIFE is gating a live studio-ops webinar behind a password
The protected session promises top-tier expertise delivered directly to studio owners and coaches — if you're in the industry, hunting down that access code is worth five minutes of your morning.
Source: body LIFE →
04
Movement is Therapy — and Wolfgang Unsöld Has the Receipts
Trainingsworld spotlights Wolfgang Unsöld's case for movement as a therapeutic tool — a timely reminder that what you're selling in your studio isn't just fitness, it's function and wellbeing.
Source: Trainingsworld →
05
Garmin Just Bought TrainingPeaks — Here's What Changes for You
Garmin has acquired TrainingPeaks, and if your clients live and die by their training plans, this merger is worth watching. Platform integrations, pricing, and data ownership could all shift — so now's a good time to know where your programming lives.
Source: Lifehacker →
06
New London gym puts recovery and wellness front and centre
London Post spotlights a brand-new gym built around injury recovery and wellness — a reminder for operators that the 'fix you up' niche is quietly becoming the whole pitch.
Source: London Post →
Stat
$200
Price of Garmin's new screen-free fitness band
It's the clearest signal yet that the no-display wearable category is becoming competitive — coaches who recommend hardware to clients now have a second credible option, and Whoop has a price-point fight on its hands.

✓ Steal: Reframe one service tier on your website around function and recovery outcomes rather than sweat metrics — 'move better, hurt less' converts differently than 'burn more.' Test it on a single class or programme description first.
✓ Try: Run a 10-minute 'movement screen' as your standard new-client intake instead of a fitness assessment — it positions you as a movement professional from session one and opens natural upsell conversations around corrective work and longevity.

DAILY

The biggest tie-up in fitness tech this year wants to 'prescribe' your workout — literally.
— Sqwod
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
EGYM & Playlist

a reported tie-up that could turn structured training into prescribed, outcome-based fitness
Connect the dots
Fitness is being rebuilt as prescribed, outcome-based medicine
A reported $7.5B tie-up between EGYM and Playlist could turn structured, data-driven training into something closer to a prescription — the right dose of the right movement for the right person. Meanwhile Planet Fitness admitted its strength pivot went too far, and Hyrox keeps globalizing competitive fitness. The market is splitting into prescribed outcomes on one end and mass participation on the other.
For operators, the EGYM–Playlist signal is the one to internalize: 'give everyone the same class' is losing to 'give this person their dose.' Personalized, measurable programming is becoming the product — and that's a game a good coach can play better than an app.
The rundown
01
EGYM and Playlist's reported $7.5B tie-up could 'prescribe' fitness
The vision: structured training that works like a prescription — the right dose for the right person. Prescribed, measurable programming is becoming the product.
Source: Athletech News →

Planet Fitness admits its strength pivot went too far
A rare public walk-back. The lesson: read your own members before chasing a trend — overshooting a pivot costs more than moving deliberately.
Source: Athletech News →

Hyrox expands its global race calendar with multi-week events
Competitive fitness as mass participation keeps scaling worldwide. If your members love a challenge, Hyrox-style events are a proven engagement and revenue engine.

The group-fitness giant is entering reformer Pilates. When Les Mills moves, thousands of studios follow — expect reformer programming to spread fast.

DAILY

Franchising is quietly betting big on two words: longevity and 'soft.'
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
Ultimate Longevity Center

sells 200 franchise territories ahead of its full launch
Connect the dots
The next franchise gold rush is longevity, not HIIT
An Ultimate Longevity Center concept sold 200 franchise territories before it even fully launched, while the industry is naming a 'soft fitness' era — recovery, mobility, and low-intensity training moving to the center. The high-burn, high-churn model is losing ground to formats people can sustain and franchisees can bank on.
For operators, this is the clearest demand signal of the summer: build for longevity and recovery, not just intensity. The consumer wants to feel better for longer — and investors are funding exactly that.

Franchisees bought in before full launch — one of the strongest demand signals of the summer. The next franchise gold rush looks like longevity, not HIIT.

The low-cost model still has runway in under-served geographies. A reminder that 'the market is saturated' is usually only true for one format at a time.

The 'soft fitness' era is officially here
Recovery, mobility, and low-intensity training are moving to the center of the offer. The stuff that used to be the cool-down is becoming the main event.
Source: Athletech News →

UFC Gym Murfreesboro opens with a recovery-first pitch
Even a combat-branded franchise is leading with full-service recovery. When the toughest names in fitness sell recovery up front, the trend has fully arrived.

200

Franchisee appetite is a leading indicator — and right now it's pointing hard at longevity and recovery over high-intensity burn.

Connect the dots
The money is moving toward prevention — and away from over-leverage
Daniel Ek's Neko Health raised $700M at a $7B valuation to scale full-body preventive scans, while lenders to a major Planet Fitness operator are reportedly in talks to take ownership. One end of the market is being rewarded for selling health before people get sick; the other is a reminder that scale built on cheap debt has a bill.
For operators, the signal is to sell prevention and outcomes, not just access. The capital — and increasingly the consumer — is chasing 'keep me well,' not 'here's a room with weights.'
The rundown
01
Neko Health raises $700M at a $7B valuation

A major franchisee's debt load is reportedly forcing a hard conversation. Proof that growth built on cheap leverage eventually sends a bill — watch your own.

NBA players sign a virtual-healthcare deal
Elite athletes putting their name to telehealth is a mainstreaming signal. Virtual health services are becoming a normal part of the performance stack, not a fringe add-on.
